chapterName: Empire: Roman Art and Architecture (c. 500 BC-AD 476)
description: Written by hand from the chapter text: the Latin words it explains

questions.question: What was the atrium of a Roman house?
questions.explanation: Aristocrats displayed their ancestors’ busts there.

questions.question: Most city dwellers lived in insulae. What were they?
options: Apartment blocks up to five storeys high
questions.explanation: The cheapest rooms were at the top, furthest from water and escape.
questions.sourceQuote: apartment blocks (*insulae*), up to five storeys high.

questions.question: What were thermae?
questions.explanation: People spent hours bathing, swimming and chatting for a tiny fee.

questions.question: What is opus caementicium?
questions.explanation: It mixed lime mortar, water and rubble with volcanic ash.

questions.question: What did a hypocaustum do?
options: Heated rooms with hot air under the floor
questions.explanation: It was a forerunner of central heating.

questions.question: What were imagines in a great Roman family?
options: Masks of the ancestors worn at funerals
questions.explanation: None survives, but many busts probably show such ancestors.
questions.sourceQuote: masks of the forebears (*imagines*) were worn in procession.

questions.question: What was the cella of a temple?
options: The main room, which housed the god’s statue
questions.explanation: Temples had a high platform with steps only at the front.
questions.sourceQuote: The main room (*cella*) housed the god's statue.

questions.question: What is an arcus triumphalis?
questions.explanation: It was one of the few building types the Romans invented.
